title: Micro-lease protocol for emergency burst and tenant isolation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and deliver a micro-lease protocol that allows tenants on Dedicated capacity to request short-lived emergency burst capacity from a shared reservoir with clear isolation, preemption, accounting, and UI/API controls. The feature should enable predictable emergency handling for customers while preserving isolation guarantees and SLAs for reserved tenants.
background: Customers using Dedicated have asked for a safe, auditable way to absorb short traffic spikes without long-term capacity commits. Existing approaches (hard overprovisioning, ad-hoc manual approvals, or global opportunistic backfill) either waste cost or risk SLA violations. We propose a micro-lease protocol: short TTL leases, negotiable preemption policies, credit accounting, and progressive isolation escalation (soft-pause -> gentle-preempt -> reclaim) to close this gap.
goals: Allow tenants to request emergency burst capacity up to a configurable cap from a shared reservoir with TTL-based leases
Provide deterministic preemption semantics and graceful degradation hooks to avoid sudden model-level interruption
Expose accounting so customers are billed or debited correctly (burst credits or on-demand pricing) and admins can audit lease history
Integrate controls in Console and API for entitlements, manual overrides, and policy tuning
Ensure isolation of reserved pools is preserved: micro-leases must never violate hard minimum allocations for active reserved tenants
non_goals: Not a long-term reservation mechanism: micro-leases expire automatically and are not intended for permanent capacity increases
Not a replacement for Dedicated contract negotiations or major capacity rebalancing
Does not include deep machine-learning based burst prediction in initial launch (telemetry will inform future work)
requirements: API: POST /v1/dedicated/leases to request a lease with params: tenant_id, max_gpus, duration_seconds, priority_tier, justification
Console: Tenant and operator views for active leases, pending requests, and historical audit logs
Reservoir scheduler: honor hard min-alloc per reserved tenant; compute safe-available capacity before granting lease
Preemption policy: three-stage escalation (soft-pause alerts to client, gentle-preempt with grace tokens, forced-reclaim) with configurable grace_seconds
Accounting: lease granularity billing events with cost breakdown (token-level cost estimate and GPU-time), and optional consumption of pre-purchased burst credits
Auditability: immutable lease records (who requested, approver, policy used, timestamps) stored for 1 year
Safety gates: automatic denial if granting would push any reserved tenant below their minimum SLA allocation
Fallback routing: if reservoir cannot grant, return structured error with suggested alternatives (queue ETA, suggested smaller lease, or mentor-mode suggestion)
Operational alerts: telemetry-based SLO for reservoir health and unexpected preemption rates
acceptance_criteria: API accepts lease requests and returns 201 with lease_id for granted leases and 409 with structured reasons for denials
Reservoir scheduler denies grants that would violate any active reserved tenant minimums in 100% of randomized tests
Console surfaces active leases and allows operator revoke with rollback grace that triggers preemption policy
Billing pipeline ingests lease events and issues correct invoice line items or applies burst-credit deductions in a staging environment
Preemption escalation executes in sequence (soft-pause -> gentle-preempt -> reclaim) with configurable grace_seconds and logs each step
Audit log contains immutable entries for 1000 simulated requests that include requester, approver (if applicable), policy id, timestamps, and cost estimate
End-to-end integration test simulating multi-tenant pressure shows no reserved tenant latency SLO violations attributable to micro-lease grants
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM interactions for billing and audit logging approved
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flags for API and Console in staging. 2) Internal beta with 3 pilot customers (operator opt-in) for 2 weeks. 3) Expand to a broader controlled cohort with telemetry gates (preemption rate, reservoir exhaustion). 4) GA when stability, billing accuracy, and isolation metrics pass thresholds.
dependencies: PM-531246 (reserve allocator and autoscale safeguards PRD)
risks: Incorrect capacity math could allow SLA violations — mitigated by staged safety checks and chaos tests
Billing mismatches on short TTL leases creating customer disputes — mitigate with end-to-end billing tests and clear invoice messaging
Operators may over-grant leases without governance — mitigate with RBAC and approval workflows
Runtime preemption may produce degraded model outputs for in-flight requests — mitigate by building graceful preemption hooks and client-visible signals
open_questions: What is the default max duration_seconds for a micro-lease? (proposal: 3600s / 1 hour)
Should there be an automatic retry/queue strategy for small denied requests or is manual user retry sufficient?
How are cross-region reservoirs handled — allow cross-region leases or restrict to region?
What SLA credit or refund policy applies if a micro-lease incorrectly causes a reserved tenant to miss SLOs?
